lawyer:
Morshed Ahmed Khan, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 

Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, Advocate—For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Jannatul Maowa Runa and others ------------ Petitioners 
Vs.
AHM Roushan Ali Miah and others ----------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
At the instance of pre-emptees in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 2002, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgement and order dated 15-11-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 2011 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgement and order dated 4-4-2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Bogra in Pre-emption Case No. 9 of 2002 allowing the pre-emption case should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this court also stayed the operation of the impugned judgement and order dated 15-11-2012 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 2011.

3. The salient facts leading to issuance of the Rule are:

4. The predecessor of the present-opposite party Nos. 1(a)-1(e) named AHM Roushan Ali Miah as pre-emptor filed the aforesaid pre-emption case for pre-empting the case land measuring an area of 17 decimals of land so described to the schedule of the petition for pre-emption.

5. The case of the pre-emptor as has been set out in this revisional application in precise is that, the case land originally belonged to one, Mofiz Pramanik and Mosirunesa. After the demise of Mosirunessa her husband, Mofiz inherited the property. While Mofiz had been enjoying title and possession over that land he transferred 10 decimals of land to one, Korban Ali on 4-9-1984. The pre-emptor then purchased 5 decimals of lands from Korban Ali on 26-11-1997 and thereby he became the co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. In further development, one Akbar Ali, the opposite party No. 4 to the pre-emption case, transferred 17 decimals of land to the opposite party No. 3 by disputed kabala that registered on 11-9-2001 though without serving any notice upon the pre-emptor-opposite party though the purchaser pre-emptees is the stranger-purchaser to the case holding. Pre-emptor came to learn about the disputed transfer on 3-10-2001 and after obtaining the certified copy of the said deed on 4-10-2011 filed the instant pre-emption case on 29-1-2002. It has further been stated in the petition for pre-emption that, if the pre-emptor had the knowledge about the said transaction. he would have purchased the same. Since the pre-emption case has been filed within the very statutory period of limitation so the pre-emptor is entitled to have the lands through pre-emption and hence the instant case.

6. Per contra, the present-petitioner as pre-emptee-purchaser contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations so made in the petition for pre-emption contending, inter alia, that, one Akbar Ali had been in possession over 30 decimals of land on mutating his name in the khatian and while he had been enjoying title and possession over that 30 decimals of land he at first proposed the pre-emptor to sell the case land even the father of the pre-emptees named, Nazrul Islam also proposed the pre-emptor and his son to purchase the land but as they refused to purchase the same, the pre-emptees then purchased the case land by registered kabala dated 11-9-2001. Soon after purchasing the case land, the pre-emptees then started enjoying title and possession over the suit properties by planting various trees that cost Taka 65,000. It has further been stated that, there has been a Madrasha located in the case land though it was not made party in the case. It has then stated that, the vendor, Korban Ali who transferred 5 decimals of land upon purchasing 10 decimals of land had separated his jama before selling 5 decimals of land to the pre-emptor. It has stated in the written objection that, inspite of having no preferential right the pre-emptor filed the case having absolute knowledge about the disputed transfer. It has further been stated that, if the pre-emption case is allowed in that event, the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 will suffer irreparable loss and injury and therefore the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed.

7. In order to dispose of the said case, the learned Assistant Judge, framed as many as 4 different issues. The pre-emptors examined 3 witnesses while the pre-emptees-petitioners examined 2 witnesses in support of their respective case.

8. Apart from that, the pre-emptor produced several documents which were marked as exhibits and on the contrary, the pre-emptees-petitioners did not produce any document in support of their cases.

9. After conclusion of the trial, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, by it judgement and order dated 4-4-2011 allowed the pre-emption case on contest against the pre-emptees-purchaser Nos. 1-3 and exparte against the rest.

10. Challenging the said judgement and order passed by the trial court, the pre-emptees-petitioners then preferred an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 2011 before the learned District Judge, Bogra. The said appeal was however on being transferred heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra.

11. The learned Joint District Judge, after hearing the parties to the appeal and on considering the materials and evidence on record ultimately dismissed the appeal and thereby affirmed the Judgement and order passed by the trial court resulting in allowing the pre-emption case.

12. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below, the pre-emptees-purchasers as petitioners then came before this court and obtained the instant Rule and order of stay as has been stated hereinabove.

13. Mr Morshed Ahmed Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the pre-emptees-petitioners submits that, both the courts below have committed a grave error of law in not considering that, the pre-emption proceedings itself was not sustainable in law, in view of the fact that the vendor had mutated his name before transferring 5 decimals of land to the present-petitioners for which the pre-emptor ceased to be any co-sharer by purchase in the case holding but that very legal point has been overlooked by the learned Judges of the courts below which has occasioned failure of justice.

14. The learned Counsel goes on to submit that, though the case was barred by the principle of waiver of acquiescence but learned Judges of the courts below did not consider the said aspect of the case when it is the clear case of the pre-emptees-petitioners that, the vendor and the father of the present-pre-emptees-purchasers at first proposed the pre-emptor to purchase the case land but as they refused to purchase the same the vendor then compelled to transfer the case land to the pre-emptees-purchasers-petitioners.

15. By filing two supplementary-affidavits, the petitioners also produced the registered kabala dated 26-11-1997 and registered kabala dated 11- 9-2001, a filed porcha bearing khatian No. 721 appertaining to plot No. 629 standing in the name of the pre-emptees-petitioners in respect of 17 decimals of land. By filing another supplementary-affidavit dated 22-11-2017, the petitioners also annexed some documents which were marked as exhibits `E1 -E2.' In another supplementary-affidavit the pre-emptees-petitioners also produced a registered kabala dated 15-7-2001 through which 20 decimals of land was transferred by the son of the pre-emptor in favour of the opposite party No. 1 Akbar Ali.

16. In support of submission, the learned Counsel has then placed his reliance in a slew of decisions reported in 19 DLR 510, 33 DLR (HC) 18, 50 DLR (AD) 97, 17 BLD 513, 12 BLC (HC) 787, 42 DLR (AD) 189, 32 DLR (AD) 55. With such submission, and relying on those decisions, the learned Counsel finally prays for making the Rule absolute on setting aside the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below.

17. Conversely, Mr Md Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel appearing for the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 (after the demise of the pre-emptor his heirs were substituted as pre-emptor-opposite party Nos. 1(a)-1(e) vehemently opposes the contention so have been advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioners and contends that, the learned Judges of the courts below have very perfectly allowed the pre-emption case finding that, all the legal requirement enumerated in section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has duly been complied with leaving no reason to interfere with the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below.

18. The learned counsel goes on to submit that, since the learned Joint District Judge, as well as the learned Senior Assistant Judge, very clearly and exhaustively discussed all the material points involved in the petition for pre-emption finding that, the pre-emption case is not barred by limitation nor it is hit by defect of parties and also it is not found to be barred by principle of waiver and acquiescence so there has been no occasion to dismiss the pre-emption proceedings.

19. The learned Counsel further submits that, since under the provision of clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act there has been gulf of difference between separation of holding and separation of jama so mere mutating the name in the khatian by the predecessor of the present-pre-emptors will not deprive the pre-emptor to exercise his statutory right of pre-emption to pre-empt the case land.

20. The learned Counsel further submits that. though the pre-emptees in its written objection allegedly stated that, before selling 5 decimals of land in favour of the pre-emptor by Korban Ali, he had mutated his name in the khatian vide mutation case but nothing of that sort of document has ever been produced by the said pre-emptees during the process of taking evidence so it clearly shows that, the mutation proceedings so have been alleged by the pre-emptees-petitioners has got no existence in the eye of law.

21. The learned Counsel further submits that, though it is alleged by the pre-emptees that, subsequent record has been prepared in the name of the pre-emptees in respect of case land, but from the record it cannot show that, the said record has finally been published in the name of the pre-emptees so until and unless a record is finally published, in that event, is cannot be said that, the holding has been separated or it recorded in the name of the pre-emptees resulting in it cannot be held that the pre-emptees have been holding possession in separate portion of land by splitting up the holding in which the pre-emptor filed the instant pre-emption case.

22. The learned Counsel lastly submits that, since all the statutory provision of law has duly been complied with by the pre-emptor in having the case land so the courts below have very perfectly allowed the pre-emption case having no occasion to interfere with the said concurrent judgement and order.

23. Anyway, in countenance of his such submission, the learned counsel has also placed a plethora of decisions so reported in 3 ALR (AD) 58, 18 BLT 83, 36 DLR 193, 2 ALR 319, 10 BLT 104, 33 DLR (AD) 205, 35 DLR (AD) 339, 39 DLR (AD) 75, 34 DLR 274 and 44 DLR (AD) 62.

24. With such submission and relying on those decisions, the learned Counsel finally prays for discharging the Rule.

25. I have considered the submission so have been advanced by the learned Counsel for the contending parties, perused the revisions) application in particular, the grounds couched thereof, the evidence adduced by the witnesses of the contending parties, the supplementary-affidavit submitted by the pre-emptees-petitioners and other materials and evidence-on-record. On the point of limitation, there has been no dispute among the parties that from the very date of knowledge, the pre-emptor filed the pre-emption case. Insofar as regards to the point of defect of parties, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, while allowing the pre-emption case has very exhaustively discussed the evidence and came to a decision that, the pre-emptor has filed the instant case within the very statutory period of limitation from the date of knowledge and no confusion can be created by the pre-emptees-petitioners upon cross examining the pre-emptor's witnesses. So far as it relates to the point of waiver and acquiescence, it is the case of the pre-emptees-purchasers that, the vendors that is, opposite party No. 2 at first offered to transfer the case land to the pre-emptor and even the father of the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 and the father-in-law of the opposite party No. 2, Mr Nazrul Islam also went to the house of the pre-emptors and even talked to his father but they refused to purchase the case land leading to the pre-emptees to purchase the case land.

26. However, that very fact so described in the written objection could not be substantiated by any of their witness though as many as 3 witnesses have been produced by the pre-emptees-petitioners, so the point of waiver and acquiescence as alleged by the pre-emptees cannot stand. Though on that very point, the learned Counsel for the petitioners has placed his reliance on the decision reported in 42 DLR (AD) 189 but the facts so have been described and the ratio so have been settled in that very decision is squarely different from that of the facts as has been stated in the instant case. Invariably, the said decision cannot be made applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case.

27. Now, only point remains, whether the pre-emptor ceased to have any right as a co-sharer by purchase to have the case land by way of purchase. It is alleged by the pre-emptees that, the vendor that is, Korban Ali before transferring 5 decimals of land infavour of the pre-emptees mutated his name in the khatian vide mutation case No. 2762 (9-1) 86/87 dated 11-11-1987 so before transferring the said case land, the khatian since has been spitted up so the pre-emptor cannot claim to be a co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. It has further been claimed by the pre-emptees that, after purchasing the case land even they also mutated their respective name in the khatian vide Mutation Case Nos. 1250, 1251 and 1252 in the year 2001 and 2002. Though there has been no mutation case number ever stated in the written objection but OPW 1 who is the father of pre-emptee purchaser No. 1 and 3 and the father in-law of the pre-emptee No. 2 has deposed that, in the month of March 2002 they got their names mutated in the khatian.

28. But curiously enough, not a scrap of paper as regards to the said mutation case infavour Korban Ali as well as the present-pre-emptees-petitioners has been produced let alone marked as exhibit by the pre-emptees while giving deposition in the case.

29. Now, for argument sake, had the vendor of the pre-emptee ever mutated his name, in that event whether the pre-emptor would have barred in exercising his right to pre-empt the case land or not. It is the contention of learned Counsel for the opposite party that, mere mutating the name in the khatian will never deprive the pre-emptor to exercise his right of pre-emption. In countenance of his submission, the learned Counsel has placed his reliance in the decision so have been reported in 3 ALR 58, which is propounded here:

Section 117(C) Sub-division of holding.

"Section 96- pre-emption of agricultural land by co-sharer or by contiguing land holder. In these cases the pre-emptees resisted the pre-emption cases on two grounds-(1) the pre-emptees after purchase of the case land have duly separated the jama of the holding and (2) the area in which the case land is situated has already been included by the Government in a municipality, thereby taking it out of the purview of section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950. The trial court accepted the contention of the pre-emptees and refused pre-emption. In revision, the High Court Division set aside the judgements of the Courts below rejecting the pleas of the pre-emptees."

30. To support that very submission, the learned Counsel for the petitioner has also placed a slew of decisions. On going through those decisions. I find that their lordship held that, if the holding is separated for paying the rent in that event, the pre-emptor will cease the right to pre-empt the case land in the said holding which is made under clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So, in view of those decisions it has been settled that, mere separating a jama, the pre-emptor will not be deprived to exercise his right of pre-emption.

<u>31. To substantiate that very submission, the learned Counsel has also placed his reliance in the decision reported in 18 BLT (HC) 83 where it has clearly been held that, as regards to point of law, the later decisions will always prevail over. Though in the decision reported in 3 ALR 58. the decision so have been given by the Hon'ble Appellate Division on that particular point made under section 117(C) has not been referred even though I find substance in it because in all along the subsequent decision always prevails over. And in the decision reported in 3 ALR it has vividly been discussed how a separation of jama and a separation of holding can be distinguished. Because, under the provision of clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, if any-person wants to separate a holding, in that event several procedure has to be performed but in the process of separating a jama which is generally called mutation in the khatian an application is simply filed before the respective Tohsil Office who then refers the same to the Assistant Commissioner (land) and the Assistant Commissioner land upon performing some procedure just mutates the khatian enabling the applicant to pay the rent in respect of his portion of land by which it cannot be said that separation of holding is held. Moreover, in separating a holding there must have some procedure to be carried out by issuing notice to all the co-sharer of the case holding but nothing of this sort has ever been complied with in the instant case.</u>

<u>32. Moreover, as has been stated herein above that, not a scrap of paper has been produced by the pre-emptees in support of separating the holding by the vendor of the pre-emptor though in the written objection the pre-emptees has stated the mutation number separating the jama by the vendor of the pre-emptees named, Korban Ali but that very paper has not been produced by the pre-emptees while giving evidence before the trial court so mere making any assertion in the written objection will not suffice to prove the case of the pre-emptees in absence of any document thereof.</u>

33. In such a panorama, the learned Counsel for the opposite party has also placed a decision with regard to the dictum per curium which has been reported in 2 ALR 319. By submitting those very decisions the learned Counsel goes on to submit that, earlier decision on the point of sub-division of holding or jama has been made as a part of per in curium for which the decision reported in 3 ALR will prevail over. And in that regard, the learned Counsel has also placed his reliance on the legal dictum (per in curium) so have been reported in 10 BLT (HC) 104.

34. I have very meticulously gone through the said 2 decisions on the point of per in curium and find every substance in it.

35. Now let me asses the contention made in two supplementary-affidavits so submitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioner one, at the time of issuance of the Rule and another, on 22-11-2017. By way of first supplementary-affidavit dated 7-2-2013 the petitioners have produced two deeds dated 26-11-1997, 11-9-2001, the khatian No. 437 when the survey reached at the stage of DP and that of the field porcha (মাঠ পর্চা) with regard to khatian No. 721 appertaining to plot No. 629 stands in the name of the present pre-emptees-petitioners. By filing those documents, the learned Counsel for the petitioners tried to give emphasis on the point that, since the present khatian number is different from that of the purchased deed of the pre-emptor dated 26-11-1997 and 11-9-2001 where the recent plot number has been mentioned as 435 and 437 so the khatian has already been changed so the pre-emptor has ceased to have any right to pre-empt the case land for having enjoyed the land that fails in separate khatian. In order to give emphasis to that, the learned Counsel has also placed his reliance in DP khatian No. 437 which has also been marked as exhibit-D-1 and that of (মাঠ পর্চা) appertaining to khatian No. 721 which has been marked as Annexure-E to the supplementary-affidavit filed on 7-12-2013.

36. Anyway, I have very meticulously gone through all those documents but I don't find any iota of substance in those documents because from those documents it does not show the said khatians have finally been published in the name of the pre-emptor or that of the name of the pre-emptees. And in that regard, the learned Counsel for the opposite party has placed his reliance on the decision reported in 36 DLR 193 where it has been held that;

Section 19 and 144:—

"In absence of final publication of record-of-right as provided in section 19 and 144 there cannot be any presumption as to its correctness."

<u>37. It has already been held that, in absence of final publication of record of right as provided in section 19 and section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act there cannot be any presumption as to the correctness. In such a view, it can safely construe that, until and unless a khatian is finally published, the pre-emptee cannot claim to have separated the holding, so that very decision is squarely applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case.</u>

38. Now let me peruse other supplementary-affidavit submitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioner in which the learned Counsel for the petitioner contends that, one of the son of the pre-emptor named, Lutfe Galif Al Zahid had earlier purchased 20 decimals of land from the vendor-opposite-party, Akbar Ali on 15-7-1999 and subsequently that very purchaser retransferred the said portion of land to the vendor, Akbar Ali on 15-7-2001. By annexing that very kabala in the supplementary-affidavit dated 22-11-2017 the learned Counsel for the petitioner wanted to impress this court that, since one of the son of the pre-emptor had earlier purchased 20 decimals of land from the case plot and re-transferred the said portion of land to the vendor, so the pre-emptor had every knowledge about the disputed transfer so have been made infavour of the pre-emptee-purchaser-petitioners. That very alleged assertion taken by the learned Counsel for the petitioner does not hold any water because the pre-emption case was filed on 11-9-2001 and that very re-transfer was made on 15-7-2001 so that very retransfer does not ifso facto prove that, pre-emptor had knowledge about the subsequent transfer. In that regard, the learned Counsel for the opposite party has relied upon a decision reported in 44 DLR (AD) 62 where it has been propounded that:

"Right of pre-emption—Waiver and acquiescence-Statutory right of pre-emption cannot be taken away by mere verbal assurance of person having such right, unless other facts and circumstances clearly make out a case of acquiescence or waiver."

<u>39. So from that very retransfer it cannot be proved that, the pre-emptor had negotiated the deal in transferring the case land in favour of the pre-emptees-purchasers so that very principle of waiver and acquiescence will not operate against the pre-emptor in exercising his right to have the case land through pre-emption.</u>

40. However, it has already been established by the decision of our Apex Court that, concurrent finding of facts cannot be interfered with if a grave error of law is apparent on the face of the record but in the instant case I don't find any such error ever been made by the learned Judges of the courts below while passing the impugned judgement because on the point of limitation, defect of parties, as well as very principle of waiver and acquiescence both the courts below found those legal points in favour of the pre-emptor which is based on assessing the evidence

and materials on record which remains uncontroverted by the pre-emptees-petitioners.

41. So only point is left for the pre-emptee-petitioners that, the pre-emptor has ceased to be any co-sharer in the case holding but no documents haw produced which will suffice to prove the said assertion. Because, though in the written objection the pre-emptees claimed that, before being transferred 5 decimals of land by the vendors of the pre-emptor, he mutated his name in the khatian mentioning a certain mutation case number but nothing of that sort document has been produced to that effect.

42. Moreover, it has already been decided by our Apex Court that, mere mutating the name in the khatian will not deprive or will not cease the right of the pre-emptor in exercising its statutory right of pre-emption.

43. So in view of the said decision so have been reported in 3 ALR, I am of the view that, the same is squarely applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case.

44. Given the above facts and circumstances and evidence and materials-on-record and the law involved in the instant case so discussed herein above, I don't find any merit in this rule.

45. The inevitable consequence that follows the Rule fails.

46. In the result, the rule is discharged, however without any order as to cost.

47. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule thus stands recalled and vacated.

Let a copy of this judgement along with the lower court records be sent to the court concerned at once.

End.
